question: A student working on a project wants to make and support a claim about whether the farm-size transition hypothesis applies to Thailand. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? Notes: The farm-size transition hypothesis holds that the economic pressures accompanying modernization drive small farms to consolidate into larger commercial operations. Masters et al. (2013): the average farm size in Asia "already has or will soon begin to rise." Promkhambut et al. (2023) contend that small rice farms in Thailand have taken up modern farming methods without any major increase in farm size. Promkhambut et al.: "The persistence of [small] rice farms [in Thailand] does not represent a `failure' to modernize...or a `truncated' transition--it is a response to modernization."
option a: The farm-size transition hypothesis may fit certain Asian countries, yet it does not match how rice farming has developed in Thailand.
option b: Masters et al. report that in Asia the average farm size "already has or will soon begin to rise," a finding that aligns with the farm-size transition hypothesis.
option c: Considered together, the studies by Masters et al. and Promkhambut et al. indicate that Thailand's rice farms have grown larger in response to the economic pressures of modernization.
option d: The anticipated shift toward large-scale commercial farming may not hold for rice farms in Thailand, where, according to Promkhambut et al., such farms have stayed small even as they've modernized.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice D uses the notes to claim the transition hypothesis may not apply to Thailand, supported by Promkhambut et al.'s finding that rice farms modernized without growing.

question: A student wants to explain why Delaware's adoption of the NPVIC matters. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? Notes: Under the Electoral College system that decides US presidential elections, whoever wins Delaware's popular vote receives all 3 of the state's electoral votes. In a 2001 article, law professors Akhil and Vikram Amar suggested that states could instead pledge their electoral votes to the winner of the national popular vote. That proposal underlies the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC). Once states controlling a majority of electoral college votes (270) adopt the NPVIC, it takes effect and adopters award their electoral votes accordingly. Delaware adopted the NPVIC in 2019.
option a: An agreement among US states to award their electoral votes to the presidential candidate who wins the national popular vote was adopted by Delaware in 2019.
option b: If the NPVIC takes effect, Delaware, as an adopter, will award all 3 of its electoral votes to the winner of the national popular vote rather than the state's.
option c: Having adopted the NPVIC, Delaware will give its electoral votes to the winner of the state's popular vote--once states holding a majority of electoral college votes (270) do the same.
option d: Under the Amars' proposal, if the NPVIC takes effect, the winner of Delaware's popular vote will receive all of the state's electoral votes.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B explains the significance by stating that, if the compact takes effect, Delaware would award all 3 electoral votes to the national popular-vote winner.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Louisa May Alcott's A Modern Mephistopheles was one of the novels in the No Name Series, a set of books released anonymously between 1876 and 1887. By daring readers to identify each book's author, the series played to the period's appetite for literary mystery. This ______ way of publishing let Alcott experiment beyond her established style.
option a: clandestine
option b: preliminary
option c: inexplicable
option d: unequivocal
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Clandestine" fits the secretive, anonymous nature of the series.

question: As used in the text, what does the word "breathes" most nearly mean? The text below is adapted from "Ojistoh," an 1895 poem by Emily Pauline Johnson, a Kanienkahagen (Mohawk) writer also known as Tekahionwake. I am Ojistoh, I am she, the wife Of him whose name breathes bravery and life And courage to the tribe who calls him chief. I am Ojistoh, his white star, and he Is land, and lake, and sky--and soul to me.
option a: Absorbs
option b: Defers
option c: Renounces
option d: Imparts
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: In context "breathes" means imparts or gives.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Although some of the specific forecasts in Alvin Toffler's 1970 book Future Shock look absurd today--we do not wear paper clothing in underwater cities--his central claim, that rapid technological and social change would leave people feeling disoriented and atomized, seems, in our own era of instability and fragmentation, remarkably ______.
option a: articulate
option b: equivocal
option c: iconoclastic
option d: prescient
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Prescient" fits Toffler's core claim proving accurate about the present.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? A definitive demonstration of the logical certainty of the sensitivity conjecture, first posed in 1992, ______ mathematicians' efforts until Hao Huang supplied the first valid proof of the conjecture in 2019.
option a: defied
option b: prefigured
option c: epitomized
option d: displaced
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Defied" conveys that a proof eluded mathematicians until 2019.

question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text? Tomi Adeyemi's debut, the inventive West African-inspired fantasy novel Children of Blood and Bone, has intriguing things to say about how identity and power relate. Adeyemi writes within a decades-old tradition traceable to authors such as Samuel Delany and Octavia Butler, who folded cultural elements of the Black diaspora into their science fiction and fantasy in a movement called Afrofuturism. At heart, the movement turns on speculation--not only about far-off futures or other worlds but also about alternate versions of our shared past. Afrofuturism's reflections on authority renew the creative possibilities of fiction.
option a: It summarizes a book, describes characteristics of the artistic movement of which the book is a part, and then points out the features the book shares with more widely read works.
option b: It introduces an intriguing debut work, contextualizes that work as part of an ongoing literary tradition, and then describes important themes of that tradition.
option c: It praises a newly published author, compares that author with others who might appear superficially similar, and then points out the features of that author's work that make it unique.
option d: It notes the political stance of an author, compares that author's book to other earlier works, and then analyzes the influence of political events on the book.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text introduces the debut, places it in the Afrofuturist tradition, then describes that tradition's themes.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? Most Native languages belong to language families--groups of languages whose structural and lexical similarities probably stem from their descent from a single language spoken long ago. A few, such as Zuni, spoken in New Mexico, and Chitimacha, spoken in Louisiana, are isolates, with no demonstrable genealogical tie to any other language. Yet Zuni and Chitimacha, like all isolates, may well be remnants of families whose other members disappeared before the historical record could document them, perhaps as extant families expanded geographically.
option a: It implies that a nonisolate language may have influenced both Zuni and Chitimacha to such a degree that their relationship to their former families is no longer discernible.
option b: It suggests that the ancestral languages of both Zuni and Chitimacha were likely isolates that replaced nonisolate languages through geographic expansion in the distant past.
option c: It proposes that the distinction made between present-day nonisolate languages and isolates like Zuni and Chitimacha may not have been applicable in the distant past.
option d: It asserts that the historical record tends to overrepresent nonisolate languages relative to isolates, such that the origins of Zuni and Chitimacha are obscure to scholars in the present day.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined sentence proposes the isolate/nonisolate distinction may not have held in the distant past.

question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the underlined portion in Text 1? Text 1: Douglas J. Levey and F. Gary Stiles observed that many migratory neotropical landbirds feed on fruit or nectar and live in forest edges and other open habitats marked by large temperature swings. They proposed that each of these traits independently helped drive the evolution of long-distance migration in many neotropical landbird species, backing the idea with data on Turdinae and other bird families. Text 2: Levey and Stiles's hypothesis leaves out another possible evolutionary precursor to long-distance migration. W. Alice Boyle and Courtney J. Conway examined data on Machetornis rixosa and 378 additional neotropical landbird species. They found that solitary foragers migrate more often than birds that forage in groups, concluding that group foraging is consistently and negatively associated with long-distance migration.
option a: By suggesting that the evolution of long-distance migration contributed in turn to changes in many birds' foraging behavior
option b: By countering that neither diet nor habitat contributed as decisively to the evolution of long-distance migration in many bird lineages as foraging behavior likely did
option c: By noting that an aspect of foraging behavior likewise may be linked to the evolution of long-distance migration in many bird lineages
option d: By recommending that more studies be conducted to determine whether there is evidence of an association between birds' foraging behavior and long-distance migration
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Text 2's author would note that an aspect of foraging behavior may also be tied to the evolution of long-distance migration.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example? Bird Species by Average Mass. Common name / Average mass (kg) / Capable of flight?: Kori bustard, 11.4, Yes; Emperor penguin, 31.5, No; Somali ostrich, 90.0, No; Wandering albatross, 11.9, Yes. Most bird species that can fly weigh under a kilogram (kg)--not surprising, given how much a flying animal is burdened by extra body weight. But not every flying bird is so light, as is clearest in the example of the ______
option a: kori bustard, which has an average mass below 10 kg.
option b: wandering albatross, which has an average mass of 11.9 kg.
option c: Somali ostrich, which has an average mass of 90.0 kg.
option d: Somali ostrich, which has a higher average mass than the emperor penguin.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The wandering albatross, at 11.9 kg, best illustrates a flying bird that is not light.

question: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Carter and Kilikoglou's argument? Researchers have examined obsidian artifacts for various purposes--to trace the long-term use of specific obsidian sources, as in Alyson Lighthart Ponomarenko's 2004 study, or to infer aspects of cultural identity, as in Dennis Ogburn and colleagues' 2009 study. Work at the Malia archaeological site on the Mediterranean island of Crete has revealed marked shifts in building styles--shifts consistent with an influx of people from another culture elsewhere in the Mediterranean--between the Middle Bronze Age and the Late Bronze Age. In a 2022 study, however, Tristan Carter and Vassilis Kilikoglou found that the methods used to make obsidian objects at Malia stayed remarkably consistent across this architectural change, which they interpret as a sign of local cultural continuity in the Middle and Late Bronze Ages.
option a: The methods used to produce obsidian objects at Malia during the Middle and Late Bronze Ages were also used by some other Mediterranean cultures in the period.
option b: Changes to buildings like those that occurred at Malia have not been linked to changes in obsidian-object production methods in other Mediterranean cultures during the Middle and Late Bronze Ages.
option c: The obsidian-object production method that was most common among other Mediterranean cultures during the Middle and Late Bronze Ages was more efficient than the method used at Malia.
option d: The obsidian used to produce objects at Malia was transported to Crete from the same source elsewhere in the Mediterranean throughout the Middle and Late Bronze Ages.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If other cultures used the same production methods, the interpretation of local cultural continuity is weakened.

question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the idea that social buffering occurs among C. helleri? In highly social mammals, the presence of others of the same species has been shown to ease stress. To test whether this effect, known as social buffering, also occurs in reptiles, a team led by Chelsea E. Martin tracked stress responses in wild southern Pacific rattlesnakes (Crotalus helleri) under three conditions: alone, with a rope, and with a companion C. helleri. The researchers compared the percent change from baseline to peak heart rate following a harmless disturbance, where higher values indicate greater stress.
option a: The average percent change in heart rate was lower among C. helleri with a companion than among solitary C. helleri and C. helleri with a rope.
option b: C. helleri with a companion displayed a lower average baseline heart rate and lower average peak heart rate than did solitary C. helleri or C. helleri with a rope.
option c: Solitary C. helleri had higher average baseline heart rates than did C. helleri in the other treatments, but the average percent change in heart rate was smaller among solitary C. helleri than among C. helleri with a companion.
option d: Average peak heart rates were highest among solitary C. helleri, but no differences were observed in average peak heart rates between C. helleri with a companion and C. helleri with a rope.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A lower percent change in heart rate with a companion indicates reduced stress, supporting social buffering.

question: Which quotation from a literary scholar would most directly support the claim in the underlined portion of the text? Scholars point to Men of Maize, the 1949 novel by Guatemalan writer Miguel Ángel Asturias, as a founding work of magical realism--the Latin American mode of fiction in which antirealistic plot devices, often taken from the spiritual and narrative traditions of Indigenous and colonial societies of the Americas, appear within the otherwise realistic representation typical of the modern novel. That style has decisively shaped authors in the United States, including Amy Tan, whose 1995 novel The Hundred Secret Senses resembles classic magical realist novels in the way it juxtaposes literary realism with long-established cultural traditions--specifically those of China and of Chinese American communities.
option a: "The cultural traditions of China as well as Chinese American communities, which figure so prominently in the magical realist tradition of Latin America, permit realistic as well as antirealistic scenarios--much as The Hundred Secret Senses does."
option b: "Although much of The Hundred Secret Senses conforms to the conventions of realistic fiction, Amy Tan also incorporates elements drawn from Chinese cultural traditions that transcend and expose the limitations of realism."
option c: "Even though The Hundred Secret Senses alternates between realistic and antirealistic modes of representation, the influence of Chinese cultural traditions remains constant throughout the novel."
option d: "Much of the interest of The Hundred Secret Senses derives from the productive tension between its competing influences--namely, Chinese cultural traditions and the magical realism of Latin America."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B shows realism juxtaposed with Chinese cultural traditions that exceed realism, supporting the claim.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Antonia Olivia Dolan and colleagues had musicians and nonmusicians, all with clinically average hearing, listen to recordings of nature sounds and of music in popular genres such as acoustic folk and orchestral, adjusting the volume to maximize their listening enjoyment. For a given recording that a musician and a nonmusician each identified as their favorite among those in the study, the researchers found that the optimal volume tended to be higher for the musician than for the nonmusician. So if a musician and a nonmusician both identified Jose Gonzalez's "Heartbeats" as their favorite recording and the musician preferred to hear it at 84.8 decibels, the nonmusician would be expected to ______
option a: not find it enjoyable to listen to any recordings at a volume as low as 84.8 decibels.
option b: prefer listening to other music at 84.8 decibels over listening to "Heartbeats" at that volume.
option c: enjoy listening to the nature sounds at 84.8 decibels more than listening to "Heartbeats" at 84.8 decibels.
option d: find listening to "Heartbeats" at 84.8 decibels less enjoyable than listening to it at a lower volume.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The nonmusician would prefer a lower volume than 84.8 dB, since musicians' optimal volume runs higher.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Pablo Picasso famously overturned the conventions of traditional painting: in his cubist works he refused to let his expression be constrained, breaking objects and figures apart to present several perspectives at once. Less well known is that Picasso--who once complained that the writers of his day had "limited themselves to moving around words somewhat while respecting the syntax"--also composed poetry that defied standard grammar, semantic relationships, and text structure. The paintings and the poems are therefore connected in that ______
option a: the poems are intended to be understood as explanations of the artistic inclinations reflected in the paintings.
option b: both exhibit Picasso's prioritization of creative expression over the standard rules of the art forms.
option c: the poems present many of the same subjects as the paintings but with different thematic approaches.
option d: both types of work are characterized by the simultaneous representation of multiple points of view that Picasso is known for.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Both paintings and poems show Picasso valuing creative expression over the standard rules of each art form.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Denmark's constitution, enacted in 1953 and made up of 6,221 words, ______ as the 13th shortest in the world--unlike Costa Rica's, which was enacted in 1949 and contains a far greater number of words (16,705). Data of this kind are studied by constitutional scholars like Dominic J. Nardi, who can use them to draw broader conclusions.
option a: rank
option b: are ranking
option c: have ranked
option d: ranks
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular subject "constitution" takes the singular verb "ranks."

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The exoplanet GJ 357 b was identified through the transit method, an indirect approach to detecting planets. Compared to that of the direct imaging method, ______ the effect these exoplanets have on nearby stars.
option a: the transit method's zone of discovery is vast, as distant exoplanets too dim to be observed are detected by
option b: distant exoplanets too dim to be observed are detected within the transit method's vast zone of discovery through
option c: the detection of distant exoplanets, too dim to be observed in the transit method's vast zone of discovery, is based on
option d: the transit method, with its vast zone of discovery, detects exoplanets that are too dim to be observed by
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A places the modifier so the compared items match and the sentence is grammatical.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In Suzhou, a city in eastern China renowned as a hub of silk production, a distinctive embroidery tradition ______ back over two thousand years--one that includes the iconic double-sided stitch, with a different image on each side--remains popular with modern audiences, preserving the city's cultural heritage.
option a: date
option b: has dated
option c: dates
option d: dating

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Indeed, the required combination of naturally occurring geological and hydrological features--accessible underground reservoirs, sufficiently high subterranean temperatures, and fractured rock--______ relatively rare, which effectively limits the Philippines' development of new geothermal energy infrastructure.
option a: proving
option b: have proved
option c: has proved
option d: are proving
subject: Reading and Writing

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Australia's early railroad network in the 1800s was notoriously uncoordinated. Trains on the broad gauge Mornington Railway line in Victoria could not run on New South Wales's narrow gauge Zig Zag Railway without time-consuming conversions. ______ historians call this tangled system the "mixed gauge muddle."
option a: Likewise,
option b: Rather,
option c: For example,
option d: Hence,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Hence" signals the conclusion drawn from the described complications.
